By virtue of the authority vested in me  
as President of the United States, it is  
hereby ordered that employees of the  
several executive departments, inde­
pendent establishments, and other gov­
ernmental agencies, including the Gen­
eral Accounting Office, the Government  
Printing Office, and the field services of  
the respective departments, establish­
ments, and agencies of the Government,  
except those who may for special public  
reasons be excluded from the provisions  
of this order by the heads of their re­
spective departments, establishments, or  
agencies, or those whose absence from  
duty would be inconsistent with the pro­
visions of existing law, shall be excused  
from duty for one-half day on Thursday,  
December 24, 1959, the day preceding  
Christmas Day; and such one-half day  
shall be considered a holiday within the  
meaning of Executive Order No. 10358 of  
June 9,1952, and of all statutes so far as  
they relate to the compensation and  
leave of employees of the United States.
The heads of departments, agencies,  
and independent establishments shall,^ to 
the extent consistent with the needs of  
the service, adopt a liberal policy for the  
granting of annual leave to all employees  
(Continued on p. 9765)

from duty for one-half day on Thursday,

leave of employees of the United States.

and independent establishments shall,^ to

the service, adopt a liberal policy for the  
granting of annual leave to all employees

versions.research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10856 (24 FR 9763, PDF pages 1-3; Federal Register issue of December 5, 1959; govinfo PDF text layer held at jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10856.txt), headed Executive Order 10856, signed by Dwight D. Eisenhower on December 3, 1959. The census register gives the same number, date and subject (Excusing Federal Employees From Duty One-Half Day on December 24, 1959). The text is an official scan read through its machine text layer; I read it for OCR damage and note below where damage matters. Inventory: the excusal paragraph excuses covered employees from duty for one-half day on Thursday, December 24, 1959, the day preceding Christmas Day, and treats that half-day as a holiday for the purposes of Executive Order 10358 of June 9, 1952 and of the compensation and leave statutes, with exceptions for employees excluded by agency heads or whose absence would be inconsistent with law. The leave-policy sentence directs agency heads, to the extent consistent with the needs of the service, to adopt a liberal policy for annual leave for employees who wish to take leave over the holiday period; it states no dates. The last paragraph says the order does not excuse employees whose posts of duty are required for national security or other public reasons. Inventory correction: the dossier's one clause runs from the order across the Register's Contents and masthead pages to the end of the order, so it includes other documents. The order itself is split by a page break (continued on p. 9765), so I use three spans: the excusal paragraph, the first part of the leave-policy sentence (up to all employees), and the second part of that sentence (who wish to take such leave over the holiday period) with the national-security exclusion paragraph. Own terms: the only stated day is December 24, 1959; the leave sentence leaves the holiday period undefined, so I record the end at the close of December 24, 1959, inclusive, and disclose the exclusive reading and a broader reading under which the leave direction would run through the unspecified holiday period. The three chosen machine searches (U.S. Code through 2026-10-09, eCFR as of 2026-10-14, Office of the Federal Register disposition notes plus operative sentences of 17521 saved order texts) each state their coverage with no warning; their coverage notes were read. They search by this order's number, and none returned a hit for it.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Candidate earlier ends examined. The only instrument the order names is Executive Order 10358 of June 9, 1952, which predates it. The Cruden number lookup in LOOKUPS.md (all held order texts except clause drafts) finds this number only in the held Federal Register text of this order itself. An exact-number search of the held text of EO 12553 (jobs/fr-originals/output/texts/EO_12553.txt, the 1986 mass revocation table) finds no entry for this number. No instrument is shown to have revoked or amended this order before December 24, 1959.","independent_command_check":"No command independent of the stated half-day: the order creates no continuing office, delegation or rule.","savings_check":"No saving wording. Pay and leave granted for the half-day are completed statutory effects, not operative commands of the order.","scope_check":"Three clauses after correction (excusal; first part of the leave sentence; second part with the exclusion paragraph). All end on December 24, 1959 by the stated day; the leave sentence is tied to the excused day and the broader reading is disclosed."}

savings_residuals.reason: The order contains no savings, exception or transitional clause; I read the whole text. Pay and leave for the excused half-day rest on the compensation and leave statutes and are completed effects; they do not keep the order operative after December 24, 1959.
